summary: The marker implementation and prior DeepGEMM artifact-identity correction pass their committed unit tests, but a compatible cache copied to a different absolute directory is not reused because DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR is included in the compatibility payload. The exhaustive warmup runs again, so the original cache-transfer contract is only partially implemented.

tests.what_was_measured: At recorded base commit, two simulated restored-cache processes invoke the all-M warmup twice and create no completion marker.

Exact candidate regression suite: marker atomicity/matching, compatibility dimensions, full DeepGEMM package/distribution artifact identity, same-path reuse, fallback, partial coverage, and compile-mode restoration; 12 passed.

Independent expected-to-pass cache-transfer contract: copy a completed cache to a different absolute path and require the same marker to skip warmup. It failed; warmup call count became 2 and a second marker was written.

gpu_execution.evidence: Hardware was probed but no GPU kernel was executed. The node exposes one AMD Instinct MI355X under ROCm 7.2; CUDA is unavailable and deep_gemm is not installed.

remaining_counterexamples: A completed compatible DeepGEMM cache copied or restored under a different DG_JIT_CACHE_DIR gets a different marker key, so exhaustive all-M warmup is repeated despite compatible artifacts.
remaining_limitations: No NVIDIA CUDA architecture was available; the assigned GPU was AMD Instinct MI355X with ROCm 7.2.
deep_gemm was not installed, so real JIT artifact generation and restoration could not be executed.
CUDA graph parity, independent NVIDIA GPU numerical results, DeepSeek-V4-Pro TP=8 startup latency, and steady-state performance remain unverified.
No native source changed in the candidate, so a native rebuild was not applicable.
